title: Allow the power-saver profile to be activated temporarily at critical battery level
line: Advanced Power Settings has a new "Switch to Power Save profile" option that puts the system in Power Save while the battery is critical and unplugged.
explanation: At the critical battery level PowerDevil only offered a final action (sleep, hibernate, shut down or nothing); the power profile stayed whatever the Low Battery profile set, so there was no way to use the strongest power saving only for the last few percent. The change adds a "Switch to Power Save profile" checkbox under "At critical level" in Advanced Power Settings (shown only when power profiles are supported, off by default). Core now only reports whether the system is on battery at or below the critical level (isBatteryCritical() and a batteryCriticalChanged signal); the PowerProfile action, which already owns the power-profiles-daemon interface, takes a HoldProfile("power-saver") while that is true and the option is on, releases it otherwise, and re-applies it after its own profile Set (which drops holds). The hold uses PowerDevil's own application id "powerdevil", and the battery applet now also looks up autostart desktop files so it shows that id as "Power Management".

commits.message:
daemon: optionally switch to Power Save at critical battery level

The critical battery level only had a final action, so the power profile
stayed the same until the battery ran out. Add an option that makes the
power profile action hold power-saver while critical and on battery.

BUG: 525875

media.caption: Master: battery at 4% (critical), the power profile stays on Balanced.
With the option on: at 4% the profile switches to Power Save, and the applet shows it was requested by Power Management because the battery level is critical.
Master: Advanced Power Settings only has the critical level action.
New "Switch to Power Save profile" checkbox under "At critical level".
